q: What comes next in the series: 1, 50, 4, 45, 7, 40, ?
x: Two interleaved series. One starts at 1 and adds 3 each time; the other starts at 50 and subtracts 5 each time. The next term is 10.

q: What comes next in the series: 3, 2, 7, 8, 11, 14, 15, ?
x: Two interleaved series. One starts at 3 and adds 4 each time; the other starts at 2 and adds 6 each time. The next term is 20.

q: What comes next in the series: 6, 60, 12, 54, 18, 48, ?
x: Two interleaved series. One starts at 6 and adds 6 each time; the other starts at 60 and subtracts 6 each time. The next term is 24.

q: What comes next in the series: 3, 4, 6, 9, 13, 18, ?
x: The gaps grow by 1 each time: 1, 2, 3... The next gap is 6, so 18 + 6 = 24.

q: What comes next in the series: 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, ?
x: Each term is the previous x 2 plus 1: 31 x 2 + 1 = 63.

q: What comes next in the series: 2, 5, 14, 41, 122, ?
x: Each term is the previous x 3 minus 1: 122 x 3 - 1 = 365.

q: What comes next in the series: 5, 7, 11, 19, 35, ?
x: Each term is the previous x 2 minus 3: 35 x 2 - 3 = 67.

q: What comes next in the series: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ?
x: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 8 + 13 = 21.

q: What comes next in the series: 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, 29, 47, ?
x: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 29 + 47 = 76.

q: What comes next in the series: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
x: Each term is a square plus 1: 1+1, 4+1, 9+1, 16+1, 25+1. The next is 36 + 1 = 37.

q: What comes next in the series: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, ?
x: These are the prime numbers in order. The next prime after 11 is 13.

q: What letter comes next: A, B, D, G, K, P, ?
x: Positions move by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 so the next step is 6: P goes to V.

q: What letter comes next: C, D, F, I, M, ?
x: Positions move by 1, 2, 3, 4 so the next step is 5: M goes to R.

q: What letter comes next: E, G, J, N, S, ?
x: Positions move by 2, 3, 4, 5 so the next step is 6: S goes to Y.

q: What letter comes next: A, Z, B, Y, C, X, ?
x: Two interleaved series: A, B, C go forward and Z, Y, X go backward. The next term is D.

q: What comes next: A1, B2, C3, D4, ?
x: Letters go A, B, C, D, E and numbers go 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

q: What comes next: AB, CD, EF, GH, ?
x: Each pair continues the alphabet from where the last pair stopped: after GH comes IJ.

q: A $80 jacket is 25% off. What is the sale price?
A $50 game is on sale for 40% off. What do you pay?
A phone costs $200 plus 10% tax. What is the total?
x: 10% of 200 is 20, so the total is 200 + 20 = 220.

q: What is 15% of 60?
20% of what number is 12?
x: 20% is one fifth. So the number is 12 x 5 = 60.

q: 30% of what number is 45?
In a class of 40 students, 35% are boys. How many girls are there?
A town of 2,000 people grows by 5%. What is the new population?
A test has 50 questions. Mia gets 80% right. How many does she get wrong?
What percent of 80 is 20?
A shirt is $40. A coupon takes off 10%, then a $2 discount is applied. What is the final price?
Four numbers have a mean of 12. Three of them are 10, 12 and 14. What is the fourth?
x: Total = 4 x 12 = 48. The three add up to 36, so the fourth is 48 - 36 = 12.

q: The mean of 5 numbers is 8. Four of them add up to 31. What is the fifth?
What is the mean of 4, 8, 9 and 15?
x: The sum is 36, and 36 / 4 = 9.

q: Scores of 70, 80 and 90 have been recorded. What score on a fourth test makes the mean 85?
x: Needed total = 4 x 85 = 340. Current total is 240, so you need 100.

q: How long does it take to drive 150 miles at 50 miles per hour?
x: Time = distance / speed = 150 / 50 = 3 hours.

q: A cyclist rides 12 miles per hour for 2.5 hours. How far does she go?
x: Distance = speed x time = 12 x 2.5 = 30 miles.

q: A train goes 240 miles in 4 hours. How far does it go in 6 hours at the same speed?
x: Speed = 240 / 4 = 60 mph. In 6 hours: 6 x 60 = 360 miles.

q: Walking at 4 mph, how many minutes does it take to walk 2 miles?
x: 2 miles / 4 mph = 0.5 hour = 30 minutes.

q: If 4 workers paint a fence in 6 hours, how long would 8 workers take at the same rate?
x: Twice the workers means half the time: 6 / 2 = 3 hours.

q: A tap fills a 60-liter tank at 5 liters per minute. How many minutes to fill it?
x: 60 / 5 = 12 minutes.

q: If today is Tuesday, which weekday will it be in 30 days?
x: 30 = 4 weeks plus 2 days. Tuesday plus 2 days is Thursday.

q: If today is Thursday, which weekday will it be in 45 days?
x: 45 = 6 weeks plus 3 days. Thursday plus 3 days is Sunday.

q: If today is Monday, which weekday will it be in 100 days?
x: 100 = 14 weeks plus 2 days. Monday plus 2 days is Wednesday.

q: If today is Saturday, which weekday will it be in 20 days?
x: 20 = 2 weeks plus 6 days. Saturday plus 6 days is Friday.

q: If today is Wednesday, which weekday will it be in 59 days?
x: 59 = 8 weeks plus 3 days. Wednesday plus 3 days is Saturday.

q: If today is Friday, which weekday will it be in 52 days?
x: 52 = 7 weeks plus 3 days. Friday plus 3 days is Monday.

q: In a non-leap year, January 1 is a Wednesday. What day is February 1?
x: January has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 days. Wednesday + 3 = Saturday.

q: If March 1 is a Monday in a non-leap year, what day is April 1?
x: March has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 days. Monday + 3 = Thursday.

q: How many days are there from March 3 to March 29, counting March 29 but not March 3?
The day before the day after tomorrow is Friday. What day is today?
x: "Day before the day after tomorrow" is tomorrow. Tomorrow is Friday, so today is Thursday.

q: A train leaves at 10:40 AM and the trip takes 2 hours 35 minutes. When does it arrive?
What is the angle between the hour and minute hands at exactly 3:00?
x: The 12 hour marks split 360 degrees into 30 each. 3 marks apart = 90 degrees.

q: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands at exactly 6:00?
x: At 6:00 the hands point in opposite directions: 6 x 30 = 180 degrees.

q: What time is 14:45 on a 24-hour clock in 12-hour time?
How many minutes are there from 8:50 AM to 11:20 AM?
x: 8:50 to 11:00 is 130 minutes, plus 20 = 150.

q: A clock chimes once at 1 o'clock, twice at 2 o'clock, and so on. How many chimes from 1 to 4 o'clock inclusive?
A clock loses 5 minutes every hour. After 6 real hours, how many minutes behind is it?
x: 6 x 5 = 30 minutes.

q: How many times a day (24 hours) does the minute hand point straight up at 12?
x: It points at 12 once per hour, so 24 times.

q: 5 people each shake hands once with every other person. How many handshakes happen?
x: Each of 5 shakes 4 hands, but each handshake is counted twice: 5 x 4 / 2 = 10.

q: 8 people each shake hands once with every other person. How many handshakes happen?
x: Each of 8 shakes 7 hands, but each handshake is counted twice: 8 x 7 / 2 = 28.

q: 10 people each shake hands once with every other person. How many handshakes happen?
x: Each of 10 shakes 9 hands, but each handshake is counted twice: 10 x 9 / 2 = 45.

q: How many diagonals does a square have?
x: A square has 2 diagonals, one joining each pair of opposite corners.

q: How many different 2-letter orders can be made from the letters A, B and C using each letter once?
x: There are 3 choices for the first letter and 2 for the second: 3 x 2 = 6.

q: A shirt comes in 3 colors and 4 sizes. How many different shirts are there?
x: 3 x 4 = 12 combinations.

q: If BED is written as CFE, how is CAT written in the same code?
x: The code moves each letter 1 place forward in the alphabet, so CAT becomes DBU.

q: If BED is written as DGF, how is DOG written in the same code?
x: The code moves each letter 2 places forward in the alphabet, so DOG becomes FQI.

q: If BED is written as CFE, how is SUN written in the same code?
x: The code moves each letter 1 place forward in the alphabet, so SUN becomes TVO.

q: If BED is written as EHG, how is MAP written in the same code?
x: The code moves each letter 3 places forward in the alphabet, so MAP becomes PDS.

q: If A=1, B=2, C=3 and so on, what is the sum of the letters in the word "CAB"?
If A=1, B=2, C=3 and so on, what is the value of the word "BED"?
If A=1, B=2 and so on, which letter has the value equal to 3 times the value of E?
x: E = 5, 3 x 5 = 15, and the 15th letter is O.

q: Ann is 3 times as old as Ben. In 6 years the sum of their ages will be 52. How old is Ben now?
x: Now: Ben b, Ann 3b. In 6 years: (3b+6)+(b+6)=52, 4b=40, b=10.

q: A mother is 27 years older than her son. In 3 years she will be 4 times his age. How old is the son now?
Two sisters are 4 years apart. Their ages add up to 20. How old is the older sister?
x: Ages x and x+4: 2x+4 = 20, x = 8. The older is 12.

q: Dan is twice as old as his brother. Together they are 18. How old is Dan?
x: Brother b, Dan 2b: 3b = 18, b = 6, Dan = 12.

q: Ann is taller than Bo. Dee is shorter than Cy. Bo is taller than Cy. Who is the second tallest?
x: The clues give the chain Ann > Bo > Cy > Dee (taller). The second tallest is Bo.

q: Kim is older than Max. Lee is younger than Raj. Max is older than Raj. Who is the youngest?
x: The clues give the chain Kim > Max > Raj > Lee (older). The youngest is Lee.

q: Ian is faster than Fay. Pat is slower than Zoe. Fay is faster than Zoe. Who is the second fastest?
x: The clues give the chain Ian > Fay > Zoe > Pat (faster). The second fastest is Fay.

q: Jon is heavier than Ivy. Gus is lighter than Hal. Ivy is heavier than Hal. Who is the lightest?
x: The clues give the chain Jon > Ivy > Hal > Gus (heavier). The lightest is Gus.

q: All zibs are yons. All yons are quas. Which must be true of every zib?
x: Zib -> yon -> qua, so every zib is a qua.

q: All cats purr. Felix is a cat. What follows?
x: Every cat purrs and Felix is a cat, so Felix purrs. The reverse is not stated.

q: If it rains, the match is canceled. The match was not canceled. What can we conclude?
x: If rain always cancels the match, then no cancellation means no rain.

q: No fish can fly. A trout is a fish. What follows?
x: No fish can fly, and a trout is a fish, so a trout cannot fly.

q: Three boxes hold a total of 30 apples. Box 1 has 4 more than box 2, and box 2 has 4 more than box 3. How many are in box 1?
x: Box 3 = x, box 2 = x+4, box 1 = x+8: 3x+12 = 30, x = 6, so box 1 has 14.

q: Only one of three keys opens a lock. You have tried two wrong keys. What is the chance the third key works?
x: Only one key works, and the other two are ruled out, so the third must work.

q: A snail climbs 3 feet up a 10-foot wall each day and slips 2 feet at night. On which day does it reach the top?
x: It gains 1 ft per full day. After 7 days it is at 7 ft. On day 8 it climbs 3 to reach 10 ft before slipping.

q: A rope is cut into 4 equal pieces with 3 cuts. How many cuts make 7 equal pieces?
x: Pieces = cuts + 1 for a rope, so 7 pieces need 6 cuts.

q: A fence has posts every 5 feet in a straight line, 8 posts in all. How long is the fence?
x: 8 posts have 7 gaps. 7 x 5 = 35 feet.

q: How many months of the year have at least 28 days?
x: Every month has 28 or more days (February has 28 or 29).

q: What is the next number in the pattern: 2, 4, 3, 6, 5, 10, 9, ?
x: The series alternates: x2 then -1. 9 x 2 = 18.

q: How many letters are between the first letter and the last letter of the word QUESTION?
x: QUESTION has 8 letters. Leave out the first and last: 8 - 2 = 6.

q: The letters of the alphabet are numbered 1 to 26. Which letter is exactly halfway between D and N?
x: D = 4, N = 14, the midpoint is 9, which is I.

q: Pen is to ink as car is to what?
x: Ink is what a pen uses up to work; fuel is what a car uses up to run.
8, 27, 64 and 125 are cubes (2, 3, 4, 5 cubed). 50 is not a cube.

q: Which is the odd one out: 21, 35, 49, 51, 63?
x: 21, 35, 49 and 63 are multiples of 7. 51 is not (7 x 7 = 49, 7 x 8 = 56).

q: Which is the odd one out: 3, 6, 9, 14, 15?
x: 3, 6, 9 and 15 are multiples of 3. 14 is not.

q: Which is the odd one out: 12, 18, 24, 30, 35?
x: 12, 18, 24 and 30 are multiples of 6 (and even). 35 is not.

q: Which position is the odd one out: April, June, January, September?
x: April, June and September have 30 days. January has 31.

q: Which position is the odd one out: Square, Cube, Circle, Triangle?
x: The others are flat 2D shapes. A cube is a solid 3D shape.

q: Cow is to calf as sheep is to what?
x: A calf is the young of a cow; a lamb is the young of a sheep.

q: Page is to book as brick is to what?
x: A page is one unit that makes up a book; a brick makes up a wall.

q: Hand is to arm as foot is to what?
x: A hand is at the end of an arm; a foot is at the end of a leg.
